subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (OmniHealth)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (OmniHealth)

Alex / Michael — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of pain & goals
- Goal: Replace legacy rule-based assistant with LLM-backed clinical-knowledge assistant for care coordinators (improve TTR, reduce manual triage).
- Primary pains: inconsistent answers across patient contexts, high per-request cost, and strict PII handling requirements for PHI.

Decision criteria (as discussed)
1) Accuracy & clinical safety (ability to tune/guardrails)
2) Latency under 350ms p95 for short prompts (<= 512 tokens)
3) Integration with internal VPC + KMS for key management
4) Pricing predictability & unit cost 
5) SOC2 + evidence for controls

Competitive landscape (vendors in bake-off)
- Redwood (us): private deployment option, KV prefix caching, quantization options, and observability.
- Vendor B: strong NLU but higher latency in our tests.
- Vendor C: cheaper per-token price but limited private deployment options.

Open questions we flagged
- Exact volume profile (avg tokens per request, expected concurrency) — Alex to confirm.
- Procurement / SOW timeline (Michael) — who needs to be looped from OmniHealth legal?
- Specific PII redaction expectations for exported logs.

Proposed evaluation (attached)
- See attached: redwood-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf — includes test cases, pass/fail criteria, and data ingestion checklist.
- Quick smoke tests we can run in 48 hours once test env is provisioned.

Next steps / owners
- OmniHealth: share sample (anonymized) prompts + volume estimate — Alex (by 2/18).
- Redwood: provision evaluation environment (VPC peering option) and share SOC2 summary — Marissa (by 2/17).
- Redwood CS: execute test plan and deliver results CSV — Rachel (kickoff 2/18).

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-test-plan.pdf

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff once we have confirmation on the data transfer method.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@omnihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (OmniHealth)

Thanks Marissa — that writeup is super helpful. A couple of clarifications: 

- Volume: we’re seeing ~2.5M requests/month now across teams but expect to start with a 200k/month pilot scoped to care coordination. Avg prompt size ~220 tokens; avg response ~300 tokens.
- Security: procurement/legal want SOC2 Type II report and a short answer on log retention/PII redaction. Can you share SOC2-Summary.pdf and confirm whether raw prompt text is stored by default?
- Timeline: procurement wants a formal SOW; Michael will own procurement questions. Can we plan the evaluation window 2/21–3/07?

Also looping in Michael (Procurement) — Michael, we’ll need to confirm billing and any required addenda for PHI processing.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the kickoff.

Alex
Sr. Product Manager, Care Ops | OmniHealth
alex.johnson@omnihealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@omnihealth.com>, Michael Torres <michael.torres@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (OmniHealth)

Alex / Michael — great, thanks for the volume details — that helps a lot. Quick responses: 

- SOC2: attaching SOC2-Summary.pdf (high-level controls + contact for detailed report). We can provide the full report under NDA — let me know if procurement needs that.
- Log retention & PII: by default, hosted logs retain request/response traces for 30 days and can be configured for zero retention in Private. For VPC/private deployments, logs can be directed to customer-managed storage and redaction can be applied at ingestion. Dylan (cc’d) will follow up with the technical notes on exact hooks for redaction.
- Evaluation window: 2/21–3/07 works on our side. We’ll provision a private evaluation environment with limited data access. 

Next steps I’ll action this week:
- Share the SOC2-Summary.pdf and the Drive folder with the test plan + onboarding checklist (link below).
- Rachel will reach out to schedule the technical kickoff and data transfer plan.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodBakeoffDocs
Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf

—
Marissa
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@omnihealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps (OmniHealth)

Alex — looping in myself as CS lead. Quick note: we have the test plan and will start the infra prep on 2/19. Action items for kickoff:

1) Alex: share a dropbox or S3 location for anonymized prompts (temp credentials) — prefer AWS S3 IAM role if possible.
2) Michael: procurement contact for SOW review; if you share the procurement contact, we’ll send a draft SOW this week.
3) Marissa/Dylan: confirm whether we should enable prefix caching for the pilot — it will reduce cost for common patient-context prompts but needs a small schema change.

I’ll send a calendar invite for 2/18 10am PT to review data ingestion and initial smoke tests. If that time doesn’t work, let me know and I’ll move it.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
